title: Transport connection optimizer & graceful retry patterns for multilang SDKs
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Problem: Customers building latency-sensitive streaming and request-heavy workloads see sporadic tail latency spikes caused by suboptimal connection pool sizing, aggressive socket teardown, and undifferentiated retry hedging across SDKs. Goal: Provide a cross-SDK transport configuration that (1) adapts connection pool and keepalive behavior to workload patterns, (2) introduces graceful hedged retry primitives for idempotent and streaming requests, and (3) ships language-specific examples and tests so app teams can adopt safe defaults without compromising throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Library default transport config that reduces tail latency by >=15% on benchmark workloads compared to current defaults
Adaptive connection pool implementation (or guidance) documented for Python/TS/Go with example config snippets
Graceful hedging primitive implemented in at least two SDKs (Python + TypeScript) with streaming reconnection semantics defined
End-to-end test harness that reproduces a 95th and 99th percentile improvement in our internal HTTP+gRPC benchmark suite
Documentation and code examples published in SDK repo and internal Confluence page
Telemetry events and dashboards created: conn_pool_size, idle_sockets_reaped, hedged_retry_count, streaming_reconnects
technical_notes: Adaptive pool sizing: maintain target_peak_utilization (default 0.75) across N routes. Pool size = ceil(mean_concurrent_requests / target_peak_utilization). Add hysteresis windows (30s) and limit delta per_rescale (max +/- 20% per resize) to avoid thrashing.

Keepalive tiers: short (5s) for low-latency internal infra, default (60s) for public endpoints, long (300s) for bursty burst-avoiding workloads. SDKs expose keepalive_profile with enumerated values: 'low-latency'|'balanced'|'burstable'.

Socket reuse heuristics: prefer reuse for streaming sessions if last_activity < stream_idle_threshold (120s). When TLS session reuse unavailable, fallback to warm-socket priming before initiating critical requests (1-2 warm connections).

Hedged retry pattern: two-stage hedging for idempotent requests: primary at t=0, hedge at t=hedge_delay (derived from p95 latency * 0.6) to avoid unnecessary duplicates. Cancel slower inflight once a faster response accepted. For streaming, implement graceful reconnect: if primary stream stalls > stream_stall_threshold (4s) open a parallel reconnect stream and bridge consumer frames deduplicating on message ids.

Backpressure and concurrency guards: per-route max_inflight (default 64) and global max_inflight derived from total GPU capacity signals for hosted runtime. SDKs should surface circuit-breaker hooks for application to observe and back off.

Telemetry: emit metrics with labels (route, model, host). Events: conn_pool_resize, conn_pruned, keepalive_profile_change, hedged_retry_fired, hedged_retry_cancelled, stream_reconnect_opened, stream_reconnect_successful. Include sample OTLP semantic conventions in docs.

Example configs: Python requests/httpx pool limits and HTTP/2 connection reuse with 'pool_limits' object; TypeScript fetch + node-agent with agent.maxSockets and keepAliveMsecs; Go net/http Transport with MaxIdleConnsPerHost and IdleConnTimeout setting examples. Provide exact snippets in repo examples folder.
test_plan: Unit tests for pool resize algorithm (edge: burst arriving when pool at min_size)
Integration: run benchmark harness with 1k concurrent clients for each SDK against a local runtime simulating varied tail latencies; assert 95th/99th reduction
Chaos: simulate long GC pauses (Python) and delayed eventloop ticks (TS) to validate hedged retry safety and duplicate suppression
Streaming: deterministic reordering test to ensure message dedupe and no data loss across reconnection bridge
Fuzz: randomize hedge_delay and target_peak_utilization to ensure we don't create infinite hedging loops
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): merge feature branches behind feature flags in Python and TypeScript SDKs; run full perf suite internally
Phase 1 (alpha): enable defaults for internal Redwood services only; monitor telemetry and SLOs for 72h
Phase 2 (beta): opt-in for external customers with SDK opt-in flag exposed; gather feedback and usage patterns
Phase 3 (GA): flip opt-in flag to default for non-streaming setups; streaming reconnect defaults gated by runtime compatibility check
Rollback: provide environment variable to revert to legacy transport behavior and an automated migration doc
implementation_tasks: PY: add adaptive_pool manager and hedged_retry orchestrator in sdk/python/redwood/transport.py (feature flag: RDW_TRANSPORT_ADAPTIVE)
TS: implement Agent wrapper examples and expose keepalive_profile in client constructor
GO: provide Transport example and guidance; prefer providing helper library functions and detailed README rather than invasive API changes
Docs: create 'Transport tuning' guide with examples, cost/latency tradeoffs, and migration checklist
Observability: add OTLP metrics and Grafana dashboard (panel templates) in infra observability repo
Benchmarks: update benchmark harness, add gating tests to CI that verify no regression on p50/p95/p99
